proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the event from
\(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}packing\text{-}comparison\text{-}same\text{-}radius}\);
uniformly over the declared union of base classes,
\[
 P(\mathcal E_n^c)\leq Cn^{-3}.                                  \tag{T1}
\]
All lists and grids are finite.  The same-radius lemma makes their
source-labeled sorting and the representative map Borel.  Empirical severity
rounding, the ordered greedy scan, first-covering-anchor assignment, finite
maximization over \(G_1(h)\), and smallest-minimizer selection over \(H_n\)
use only finitely many Borel comparisons and arithmetic operations.
Second-half counts and sums are Borel, their zero-count branches are
explicit, and both projections are continuous.  Thus
\((O_1,\ldots,O_n,x)\mapsto\widehat\tau_n(x)\) is Borel.  The supremum loss
is measurable because the construction has finitely many sample-dependent
cells and \(\tau_P\) is continuous by the Lipschitz assumption.  The formula
contains neither \(\kappa\) nor a class label.

For \(h\in H_n\), define
\[
 V_P(h)=\sup_{x\in B}\left[
 Lh+\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log\!\left(
 e\{1\vee J_P(h,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h)\})\}\right)}
 {na_P(x,h)}}\right],
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_P=\min_{h\in H_n}V_P(h).                              \tag{T2}
\]
The base-mass assumption gives
\(a_P(x,h)\geq c_mh^\kappa>0\), so all divisions and logarithms in
\((\mathrm{T2})\) are well defined.  Choose \(C_0\) larger than the
numerical constant in the severity-net population comparison.

We first compare criteria in the informative regime.  Let \(h\) satisfy
\[
 n_1\inf_{x\in B}a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en).                          \tag{T3}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \((\mathrm{P3})\), the exact empirical-pattern identity
at \(x\) and \(g_h(x)\), and the second conclusion of the severity-net lemma
give, for every \(x\),
\[
 a^L(g_h(x),h)\geq\tfrac12a_P(x,h),\qquad
 Z_n(g_h(x),h)
 \leq C\left[1+\log\!\left(
 e\{1\vee J_P(h,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h)\})\}\right)\right].           \tag{T4}
\]
Since every \(g\in G_1(h)\) is its own representative, maximizing
\((\mathrm{T4})\) over \(g\) shows that, whenever the right side of
\((\mathrm{T4})\) also makes the admissibility inequalities hold,
\[
 \widehat V(h)\leq C V_P(h).                                     \tag{T5}
\]

Let \(h_\star\) attain the finite minimum in \((\mathrm{T2})\), and put
\(\ell=\log(en)\).  Suppose first that
\[
 \mathcal R_P<c_\star\sigma/\sqrt{\ell},                         \tag{T6}
\]
where \(c_\star>0\) is a sufficiently small numerical constant.
 Write \(z_P(x,h_\star)\) for the logarithmic numerator in
 \((\mathrm{T2})\).  The variance term is at most \(\mathcal R_P\), and
 \(z_P(x,h_\star)\geq1\), so
\[
 \frac{na_P(x,h_\star)}{z_P(x,h_\star)}
 \geq\frac{\sigma^2}{\mathcal R_P^2}
 >c_\star^{-2}\ell,
 \qquad
 na_P(x,h_\star)>c_\star^{-2}\ell
 \quad\text{for every }x\in B.                                  \tag{T7}
\]
Because \(n_1\asymp n_2\asymp n\) for \(n\geq2\), taking \(c_\star\)
small enough makes \((\mathrm{T3})\) and all admissibility inequalities
follow from \((\mathrm{T4})\) and \((\mathrm{T7})\).  Thus
\[
 \widehat V(\widehat h)\leq\widehat V(h_\star)
 \leq C\mathcal R_P
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_n.                                   \tag{T8}
\]

For completeness, the complementary regime does not require an unstated
mass assumption.  Suppose
\(\mathcal R_P\geq c_\star\sigma/\sqrt{\ell}\).
For all sufficiently large \(n\), choose \(h_s\in H_n\) with
\[
 (\ell^2/n)^{1/\kappa}\leq h_s<2(\ell^2/n)^{1/\kappa};            \tag{T9}
\]
the compact exponent window and \(h_0>0\) make this possible uniformly.
The base-mass assumption gives
\[
 \inf_xa_P(x,h_s)\geq c_mh_s^\kappa\geq c_m\ell^2/n.             \tag{T10}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \((\mathrm{P3})\) applies.  Independently of the law,
an \(h_s/2\)-separated subset of the unit-length segment \(B\) has at most
\(1+2/h_s\) points.  Hence
\[
 \max_g Z_n(g,h_s)\leq C\log(e/h_s)\leq C\ell.                   \tag{T11}
\]
Equations \((\mathrm{T10})\)--\((\mathrm{T11})\) make \(h_s\) admissible and
give
\[
 \widehat V(h_s)
 \leq CL(\ell^2/n)^{1/\kappa}+C\sigma/\sqrt{\ell}
 \leq C\sigma/\sqrt{\ell}
 \leq C\mathcal R_P,                                             \tag{T12}
\]
where the penultimate inequality holds uniformly for
\(\kappa\in[2+\epsilon,\bar\kappa]\) once \(n\) is large; its constant may
depend on the fixed ratio \(L/\sigma\).  Therefore \((\mathrm{T8})\) also
holds in this regime.  The finitely many remaining \(n\) are absorbed by
enlarging \(C\): projection bounds the loss by \(4L\), while
\(\mathcal R_P\geq\sigma/\sqrt n\).

On \(\mathcal E_n\), at least one bandwidth is admissible by the preceding
dichotomy, so \(\widehat h\) is the ordinary smallest minimizer and is
\(I_1\)-measurable.  Invoke the conditional conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}severity\text{-}net\text{-}extension}\)
at this single bandwidth.  Equations \((\mathrm{T8})\) and the tower
property yield
\[
 E_P[\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\mathbf1_{\mathcal E_n}]
 \leq C\mathcal R_P.                                              \tag{T13}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n^c\), both the projected estimator and the target take
values in \([-2L,2L]\), so \((\mathrm{T1})\) bounds the contribution by
\(4LCn^{-3}\).  Since
\(n^{-3}\leq\log^2(en)/n\), combining this with
\((\mathrm{T2})\) and \((\mathrm{T13})\) proves the displayed oracle
inequality.  In particular, the infimum is outside the boundary supremum
because one global bandwidth is used.

The revised construction contains neither \(\kappa\) nor either endpoint
class label.  We evaluate the proved global-bandwidth oracle with one common
bandwidth in each class.

Fix \(\kappa\in K\).  For the isolated class, put
\(b=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and for all sufficiently large \(n\) choose
\(h_b\in H_n\) with \(b\leq h_b<2b\).  For \(x\in B\), write
\[
 a_P(x,h_b)=w_xh_b^\kappa.
\]
The base-mass assumption gives \(w_x\geq c_m\).  Enlarge the fixed oracle
constant \(C_0\) so that \(C_0c_m\geq C_m\), and write
\(\alpha=\kappa-2\).  If \(C_0w_xh_b^\kappa\leq1\), the isolated-envelope
assumption gives
\[
 J_P(h_b,C_0a_P(x,h_b))
 \leq C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+Cw_x^{1/\alpha}\}.                     \tag{E1}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 h_b^{-1}\left(\frac{C_0w_xh_b^\kappa}{h_b^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}
 =C_0^{1/\alpha}w_x^{1/\alpha}.
\]
If \(C_0w_xh_b^\kappa>1\), apply the same envelope at \(u=1\).
The premise implies
\[
 w_x^{1/\alpha}\geq
 C_0^{-1/\alpha}h_b^{-\kappa/\alpha}
 =C_0^{-1/\alpha}h_b^{-1-2/\alpha},
\]
so \((\mathrm{E1})\) remains valid with the clipped threshold.  Since
\(\alpha\in[\epsilon,\bar\kappa-2]\),
\[
 \sup_{\alpha\in[\epsilon,\bar\kappa-2]}
 \sup_{w\geq c_m}
 \frac{1+\log[e\{1+C(1+w^{1/\alpha})\}]}{w}<\infty.              \tag{E2}
\]
Also \(nh_b^\kappa\asymp h_b^{-2}\).  Hence \((\mathrm{E1})\)--\((\mathrm{E2})\)
give uniformly in \(x,P,\kappa\),
\[
 Lh_b+\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log[e\{1\vee
 J_P(h_b,\min(1,C_0a_P(x,h_b)))\}]}
 {na_P(x,h_b)}}
 \leq Cb.                                                        \tag{E3}
\]
The theorem remainder is \(o(b)\), uniformly on the compact exponent
window.  Taking the supremum in \(x\) and then the theorem's bandwidth
infimum proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq Cn^{-1/(\kappa+2)}.                                       \tag{E4}
\]

For the pervasive endpoint, the following argument in fact holds on all of
\(\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\).  Every \(h\)-separated subset of the unit-length
segment \(B\) has cardinality at most \(1+1/h\leq2/h\), because
\(h\leq h_0\leq1/8\).  Therefore
\[
 1\vee J_P(h,u)\leq2/h                                           \tag{E5}
\]
for every \(u\geq0\).  Put
\(r=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and choose
\(h_r\in H_n\) with \(r\leq h_r<2r\).  By the base-mass assumption and
\((\mathrm{E5})\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{x\in B}\left[
 Lh_r+\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log[e\{1\vee
 J_P(h_r,\min(1,C_0a_P(x,h_r)))\}]}
 {na_P(x,h_r)}}\right]
 &\leq CLh_r+
 C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e/h_r)}{nc_mh_r^\kappa}}\\
 &\leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.                              \tag{E6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The theorem remainder is again smaller uniformly on \(K\).
Since \(\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\subseteq\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.                               \tag{E7}
\]
The identical total estimator occurs in \((\mathrm{E4})\) and
\((\mathrm{E7})\), which proves simultaneous endpoint adaptation.

Put \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell=\log(en)\).  When \(m=0\), the condition
\(mu\geq C\ell\) has no solutions, and the definitions give
\(q_t^L=0\leq q_t\leq1=q_t^U\), hence \((\mathrm{P2})\).  We may therefore
assume \(m\geq1\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(s\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(h\in H_n\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_{t,s,h}
 =\{z\in A_t:\|z-(0,s)\|_2\leq h\}.
\]
For deterministic \(z_i=(r_i,s_i)\), membership of \(z_i\) in this set,
as a function of \(s\), is zero unless \(z_i\in A_t\) and \(|r_i|\leq h\);
otherwise it is the indicator of the closed interval
\[
 [s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},\,s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}].                  \tag{P4}
\]
Thus the trace on \(N\) points changes only at at most \(2N\) endpoints.
Since \(|H_n|\leq2+\log_2n\), the shatter coefficient of
\[
 \mathcal C_n=\{\mathcal C_{t,s,h}:t\in\{0,1\},
 \ s\in[-1/2,1/2],\ h\in H_n\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(N)
 \leq2|H_n|(2N+1)\leq C_0(N+1)\ell.                              \tag{P5}
\]

We prove the relative empirical inequality used below.  For a measurable
set class \(\mathcal A\), an empirical law \(P_m\) based on \(m\) independent
observations, and
\(\Gamma=x+\log\{8\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\}\), \(x\geq1\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal A:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2P_m(C)\Gamma}{m}}+\frac{7\Gamma}{3m}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}.                                                     \tag{P6}
\]
To derive it, introduce an independent empirical law \(P'_m\), condition on
the pooled \(2m\) observations, pair them, and independently choose which
member of each pair enters \(P_m\).  For a fixed pooled trace, the difference
of its two counts is a sum of independent signs over at most
\(2m\bar p\) discordant pairs, where
\(\bar p=(P_m(C)+P'_m(C))/2\).  The identity
\(\cosh(v)\leq e^{v^2/2}\), exponential Markov, and optimization give
\[
 \Pr\{|P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|>2\sqrt{\bar pz/m}\mid\text{pooled sample}\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                     \tag{P7}
\]
Peel \(\bar p\) into \(2^{-j-1}<\bar p\leq2^{-j}\), use
\(z=\Gamma+(j+1)\log2\), and union over at most
\(\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\) traces.  The probabilities sum geometrically.
For the ghost-sample reduction, if
\(d=|P_m(C)-P(C)|\) violates \((\mathrm{P6})\), the independent ghost half
has conditional probability at least \(1/4\) of satisfying
\[
 |P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|
 >\sqrt{4\bar p\Gamma/m}+2\Gamma/(3m).
\]
This follows on substituting \(P(C)\leq P_m(C)+d\) for a downward deviation,
\(P(C)\leq P_m(C)\) for an upward deviation, and using
\(2\sqrt{d\Gamma/m}\leq d/2+2\Gamma/m\).  Multiplication by four proves
\((\mathrm{P6})\).  The argument uses only pooled traces, so increasing
finite trace subfamilies covers a nonattained supremum.

Apply \((\mathrm{P6})\) to \(\mathcal C_n\) with \(x=3\ell\).
By \((\mathrm{P5})\), \(\Gamma\leq6\ell\) for \(n\geq2\), and hence
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal C_n:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{12P_m(C)\ell/m}+20\ell/m\right\}
 \leq C_1n^{-3}.                                                   \tag{P8}
\]
The closed intervals in \((\mathrm{P4})\) include traces attained at all
breakpoint ties.  Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the complement of this event.
Since \(P_m(\mathcal C_{t,s,h})=\widehat q_t^{(1)}((0,s),h)\),
\((\mathrm{P8})\) and the definitions imply
\[
 q_t^L(x,h)\leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)                           \tag{P9}
\]
simultaneously in \(x,t,h\), and taking minima proves \((\mathrm{P2})\).
If \(mq_t(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), solving the two quadratic inequalities in
\((\mathrm{P8})\) gives
\[
 \tfrac12q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^L(x,h)
 \leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)\leq2q_t(x,h).                       \tag{P10}
\]
When \(ma_P(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), this holds on both sides, and taking minima
proves \((\mathrm{P3})\).

Fix \(h\).  Every endpoint in \((\mathrm{P4})\) generated by a first-half
score and lying in the target segment occurs in the source-labeled list.
Lexicographic order is total, and retaining the least label at equal
coordinates retains the common breakpoint.  A deterministic mesh point tied
with a breakpoint likewise occurs once.  Define \(g_h((0,s))=(0,s)\) at
each listed coordinate and otherwise map \(s\) to the midpoint of its unique
open cell.  No first-half membership indicator changes in an open cell.
Because \(M_h=\lceil16/h\rceil\), consecutive deterministic mesh points are
at distance at most \(h/16\).  Therefore, including at every tie,
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2\leq h/32<h/4,\qquad
 \widehat q_t^{(1)}(g_h(x),h)=\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h).             \tag{P11}
\]

Let \(F\) be \(h\)-separated and contained in
\(\{x:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\).  For each \(x\in F\), choose \(t_x\) with
\(q_{t_x}(x,h)\leq u\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\), putting
\(z=\widehat q_{t_x}^{(1)}(x,h)\) in \((\mathrm{P8})\) and solving gives
\(z\leq2u+64\ell/m\).  Applying the definition of \(b_n\) and
\(2\sqrt{uv}\leq u+v\), then using \((\mathrm{P11})\), yields
\[
 a^U(g_h(x),h)\leq C_3\{u+\ell/m\}.                               \tag{P12}
\]
For distinct \(x,x'\in F\),
\[
 \|g_h(x)-g_h(x')\|_2\geq h-h/32-h/32=15h/16>h/2.                \tag{P13}
\]
The upward rounding satisfies
\[
 u(v)\leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\},                                    \tag{P14}
\]
including \(v=0\), directly from adjacent dyadic ratio two and the smallest
positive grid value.  Choosing the numerical \(c\) large enough makes
\(g_h(F)\) feasible for
\(\widehat J(h,c\{u+\ell/m\})\); \((\mathrm{P13})\) makes the map injective.
Taking the maximum proves the first inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\), also
when \(u=1\).

Conversely, let \(G\) be nonempty and feasible in \(\widehat J(h,v)\).
Equations \((\mathrm{P2})\) and \((\mathrm{P14})\) give
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\leq u(v)
 \leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\},\qquad g\in G.                           \tag{P15}
\]
Order \(G=\{g_1<\cdots<g_M\}\) on \(B\).  Feasibility and collinearity give
\[
 \|g_{j+2}-g_j\|_2
 =\|g_{j+2}-g_{j+1}\|_2+\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h.                 \tag{P16}
\]
The odd and even sublists are thus \(h\)-separated at the same physical
radius \(h\), and \((\mathrm{P15})\) makes both feasible for the population
packing.  Hence
\[
 |G|\leq2J_P(h,\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\}).                             \tag{P17}
\]
If the finite maximum is empty, the outer floor is one.  Substitute
\(v=c\{u+\ell/m\}\), enlarge \(C\), and combine the two cases to prove the
upper inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\) with \(1\vee J_P\).  No radius
monotonicity has been used.

Finally, the square-root endpoint map is continuous on its closed domain.
Candidate inclusion, lexicographic comparisons, finite sorting, least-label
tie removal, deterministic refinement, and midpoint formation are Borel.
The finite maximum defining \(\widehat J\) is a maximum of finitely many
Borel feasibility indicators after absent slots are encoded by their Borel
presence indicators.  This proves all measurability assertions and completes
the proof.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the event in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}packing\text{-}comparison\text{-}same\text{-}radius}\).
For every \(\kappa\in K\), \(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), and the constants in \(\mathrm{def{:}profile\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\), the following hold on \(\mathcal E_n\).  First, for every \(h\in H_n\), \(v\in U_n\), and \(x\in B\),
\[
 |\mathcal A_1(h,v)|
 \leq
 \widehat J\!\left(h,128\left\{v+\frac{\log(en)}{n_1\vee1}\right\}\right),
 \qquad
 \|x-\gamma_1(x,h)\|_2<\frac{33h}{32}.
\]
Second, if \(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\), then
\[
 \widehat J\!\left(
 h,128\left\{\widehat u(g_h(x),h)+
 \frac{\log(en)}{n_1\vee1}\right\}\right)
 \leq C\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h)\}\right)\right\}.
\]
Third, if \(h\) is admissible, then, conditionally on \(I_1\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[
 \|\widehat\tau_{n,h}-\tau_P\|_\infty\mid I_1\right]
 \leq C\widehat V(h).
\]
The constants are uniform over \(\kappa\in K\).  No union over \(H_n\) occurs in the last inequality because \(h\) is fixed conditionally on \(I_1\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(m=n_1\), \(r_n=\log(en)/(m\vee1)\), and fix \(h\in H_n\).
The representative construction in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}packing\text{-}comparison\text{-}same\text{-}radius}\)
gives, including at every breakpoint tie,
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2\leq h/32,\qquad
 \widehat q^{(1)}_t(g_h(x),h)=\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h),
 \quad t=0,1.                                                     \tag{S1}
\]
Thus \(a^L\), \(a^U\), and \(\widehat u\) agree at \(x\) and \(g_h(x)\).
The ordered greedy rule is maximal in each finite band.  Its anchors are
\(h\)-separated, and every member of the band not retained is at distance
strictly less than \(h\) from an earlier retained anchor.  Hence the first
covering anchor exists and
\[
 \|x-\gamma_1(x,h)\|_2
 \leq\|x-g_h(x)\|_2+\|g_h(x)-\gamma_1(x,h)\|_2
 <33h/32.                                                        \tag{S2}
\]

We next control the size of an anchor band.  Put
\(b(z)=\sqrt{12zr_n}+20r_n\).  If
\(d=\max\{0,z-b(z)\}\), then
\[
 \min\{1,z+b(z)\}\leq128(d+r_n).                                 \tag{S3}
\]
Indeed, when \(d=0\), \(z\leq\sqrt{12zr_n}+20r_n\); solving this quadratic
gives \(z\leq43r_n\), and then \(z+b(z)\leq86r_n\).
When \(d>0\), \(z=d+b(z)\), and
\[
 b(z)\leq\sqrt{12dr_n}+\sqrt{12b(z)r_n}+20r_n
 \leq\sqrt{12dr_n}+\frac{b(z)}2+26r_n.
\]
Therefore \(b(z)\leq2\sqrt{12dr_n}+52r_n\leq d+64r_n\), proving
\((\mathrm{S3})\).  Choose a side attaining
\(a^L(g,h)=\min_tq^L_t(g,h)\) and apply \((\mathrm{S3})\) to its empirical
mass.  This yields
\[
 a^U(g,h)\leq128\{a^L(g,h)+r_n\}.                                \tag{S4}
\]
If \(g\in\mathcal A_1(h,v)\), then \(a^L(g,h)\leq v\).
Equations \((\mathrm{S4})\) and the cap built into the rounding map \(u\)
show that this anchor set is feasible for the maximum defining
\(\widehat J(h,128\{v+r_n\})\).  Its \(h\)-separation is stronger than the
required \(h/2\)-separation, proving the asserted cardinality bound.

For the population comparison, suppose \(ma_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\).
By \((\mathrm{S1})\) and the relative inequalities \((\mathrm{P3})\) from
the same-radius lemma, both \(a_P(x,h)\) and \(a_P(g_h(x),h)\) lie between
\(a^L(g_h(x),h)\) and twice that quantity.  The positive dyadic rounding
therefore gives
\[
 \widehat u(g_h(x),h)\leq2a^L(g_h(x),h)\leq2a_P(x,h),
 \qquad r_n\leq C a_P(x,h).                                      \tag{S5}
\]
Let \(G\) be feasible in the definition of
\(\widehat J(h,128\{\widehat u(g_h(x),h)+r_n\})\).
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \((\mathrm{P2})\) implies that every \(g\in G\) obeys
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)
 \leq u\!\left(128\{\widehat u(g_h(x),h)+r_n\}\right)
 \leq\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h)\},                                        \tag{S6}
\]
where the last inequality follows from
\(u(w)\leq\min\{1,2w+(m\vee1)^{-1}\}\) and \((\mathrm{S5})\).
Ordering \(G\) along the line \(B\), its odd and even sublists are
\(h\)-separated because adjacent points of \(G\) are \(h/2\)-separated.
Each sublist is therefore feasible for the population packing in
\((\mathrm{S6})\), and
\[
 |G|\leq2J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h)\}\right).
\]
If the finite maximum is empty, the outer floor equals one.  Combining the
two cases proves the second assertion with \(1\vee J_P\).

It remains to prove the stochastic assertion.  Condition on \(I_1\); the
bandwidth \(h\), all anchor sets, and all assignments are now fixed.
For \(a\in\mathcal A_1(h,v)\), let
\[
 q_t(a,h)=P\{X\in A_t,\ \|X-a\|_2\leq h\},
 \qquad
 M_v=|\mathcal A_1(h,v)|,
\]
and put
\[
 Z_v=1+\log\!\left[
 e\widehat J\!\left(h,128\{v+r_n\}\right)\right].
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \((\mathrm{P2})\) gives
\[
 q_t(a,h)\geq a_P(a,h)\geq a^L(a,h).                             \tag{S7}
\]
If \(h\) is admissible, no anchor belongs to the zero band.  Nor can an
anchor belong to the smallest positive band: its upper endpoint is at most
\((m\vee1)^{-1}\), whereas \(n_2/(m\vee1)\leq2\) for \(n\geq2\), contradicting
\(n_2a^L(a,h)\geq2^{14}Z_v\) and \(Z_v\geq2\).
Consequently, in every nonempty anchor band,
\[
 v/2<a^L(a,h)\leq v,\qquad M_v\leq e^{Z_v-1}.                    \tag{S8}
\]

Define
\[
 K_h=\max_{g\in G_1(h)}
 \sqrt{\frac{Z_n(g,h)}{n_2a^L(g,h)}}.
\]
Order the nonempty positive bands as \(v_0<\cdots<v_J\).
They are dyadic, so \(v_j\geq2^jv_0\).  By \((\mathrm{S8})\), for every
anchor and side, the binomial Chernoff calculation gives
\[
 P\{N^{(2)}_t(a,h)<n_2v_j/4\mid I_1\}
 \leq\exp(-n_2v_j/16).                                           \tag{S9}
\]
This follows directly from
\(E[e^{-\lambda N}\mid I_1]=(1-q+qe^{-\lambda})^{n_2}\),
\(\log(1+w)\leq w\), and optimization at
\(e^{-\lambda}=1/2\), using \(q\geq v_j/2\).
Admissibility and \((\mathrm{S8})\) imply both
\(n_2v_j\geq2^{14}Z_v\) and
\(n_2v_j\geq2^jn_2v_0\).  A union bound in \((a,t,j)\) therefore gives
\[
 P\{\text{\((\mathrm{S9})\) fails for some anchor and side}\mid I_1\}
 \leq C\exp(-c n_2v_0).                                         \tag{S10}
\]

For \(i\in I_2\), set
\[
 \varepsilon_i
 =Y_i-T_im_{1,P}(X_i)-(1-T_i)m_{0,P}(X_i).
\]
Independence and the conditional sub-Gaussian assumption imply, conditional
on all second-half scores, that every average over a nonempty fixed index
set \(A\) satisfies
\[
 P\!\left\{\left|\frac1{|A|}\sum_{i\in A}\varepsilon_i\right|
 >\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2z}{|A|}}\ \middle|\ X_i,\ i\in I_2\right\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                     \tag{S11}
\]
On the count event in \((\mathrm{S10})\), apply \((\mathrm{S11})\) in band
\(j\) with \(z=4(Z_v+3j+s)\), then take a union over the two sides and the
\(M_v\) anchors.  Since \(M_v\leq e^{Z_v-1}\),
\[
 P\!\left\{
 \max_{j,a,t}\left|
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-a\|_2\leq h\}}
 {N^{(2)}_t(a,h)}
 \right|
 >C\sigma\max_j
 \sqrt{\frac{Z_v+j+s}{n_2v_j}}
 \ \middle|\ I_1\right\}
 \leq Ce^{-s}.                                                     \tag{S12}
\]
There is no bandwidth union in this calculation.

Choose an anchor in the lowest nonempty band.  By \((\mathrm{S8})\),
\[
 K_h^2\geq\frac1{n_2v_0}.
\]
Also \(Z_v/(n_2v_j)\leq K_h^2\), and
\[
 \frac{j}{n_2v_j}\leq
 \frac{j2^{-j}}{n_2v_0}\leq CK_h^2,
 \qquad
 \frac{s}{n_2v_j}\leq sK_h^2.                                   \tag{S13}
\]
Thus the threshold in \((\mathrm{S12})\) is at most
\(C\sigma K_h\sqrt{1+s}\).  Integrating the tail in \(s\) yields an expected
maximum at most \(C\sigma K_h\).  The exceptional count probability in
\((\mathrm{S10})\) is also on this scale, because
\[
 e^{-c n_2v_0}\leq C(n_2v_0)^{-1/2}\leq CK_h.                    \tag{S14}
\]
The estimator and target both lie in \([-2L,2L]\), so its contribution is
at most \(C L K_h\), which is \(C\sigma K_h\) with the allowed dependence
of \(C\) on the fixed ratio \(L/\sigma\).

Finally, if \(N^{(2)}_t(a,h)>0\), every included score lies within \(h\) of
\(a=\gamma_1(x,h)\).  By \((\mathrm{S2})\) and the Lipschitz assumption,
\[
 \left|
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_2}m_{t,P}(X_i)
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-a\|_2\leq h\}}
 {N^{(2)}_t(a,h)}
 -\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \leq\frac{65}{32}Lh.                                             \tag{S15}
\]
All points used in \((\mathrm{S15})\) lie in the closed \(h_0\)-neighborhood
of \(B\), as required by the Lipschitz assumption.  The trace-envelope
assumption places \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\) in \([-L,L]\), so projection onto
\([-L,L]\), and then projection of the contrast onto \([-2L,2L]\), cannot
increase the error.  Summing \((\mathrm{S15})\) over the two sides and using
\((\mathrm{S12})\)--\((\mathrm{S14})\) gives
\[
 E_P[\|\widehat\tau_{n,h}-\tau_P\|_\infty\mid I_1]
 \leq C\{Lh+\sigma K_h\}\leq C\widehat V(h),
\]
which proves the lemma.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell_n=\log(en)\), and split the observations into \(I_1\) and \(I_2\).  Let
\[
 H_n=\{h_02^{-j}:0\leq j\leq\lceil\log_2n\rceil\},
 \qquad
 U_n=\{0,1\}\cup
 \{2^{-\ell}:0\leq\ell\leq\lceil\log_2(m\vee1)\rceil\}.
\]
On \(I_1\), set
\[
 \widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h)
 =(m\vee1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}
 \mathbf 1\{X_i\in A_t,\ \|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\},
 \qquad
 b_n(v)=\sqrt{\frac{12v\ell_n}{m\vee1}}
       +\frac{20\ell_n}{m\vee1},
\]
\[
 q^U_t(x,h)=\min\{1,\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h)+b_n(\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h))\},
 \quad
 q^L_t(x,h)=\max\{0,\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h)-b_n(\widehat q^{(1)}_t(x,h))\},
\]
and \(a^U(x,h)=\min_tq^U_t(x,h)\), \(a^L(x,h)=\min_tq^L_t(x,h)\).

For \(h\in H_n\), form the source-labeled list consisting of
\((-1/2,0,0)\), \((1/2,0,1)\), and every
\[
 \left(S_i+e\sqrt{h^2-R_i^2},i,e\right),
 \qquad i\in I_1,\quad e\in\{-1,1\},
\]
for which \(|R_i|\leq h\) and
\(S_i+e\sqrt{h^2-R_i^2}\in[-1/2,1/2]\).
Sort lexicographically by boundary coordinate, then by \(i\), then by \(e\),
and at repeated coordinates retain the least source label.  Write the
remaining coordinates as
\(-1/2=z_0<\cdots<z_M=1/2\), and set
\[
 C_1(h)=((0,z_0),\ldots,(0,z_M)).
\]
Put \(M_h=\lceil16/h\rceil\), sort the union
\[
 \{z_0,\ldots,z_M\}\cup
 \{-1/2+j/M_h:0\leq j\leq M_h\}
\]
as \(-1/2=w_0<\cdots<w_Q=1/2\), and define
\[
 G_1(h)=\{(0,w_j):0\leq j\leq Q\}
 \cup
 \left\{\left(0,\frac{w_j+w_{j+1}}2\right):0\leq j<Q\right\}.
\]
For \(x=(0,s)\in B\), define \(g_h(x)=x\) if \(s=w_j\) for some \(j\);
otherwise, for the unique \(j\) with \(w_j<s<w_{j+1}\), define
\[
 g_h(x)=\left(0,\frac{w_j+w_{j+1}}2\right).
\]

For \(v\geq0\), let \(u(v)\) be the smallest element of \(U_n\) at least
\(\min\{1,v\}\), and set
\[
 \widehat J(h,v)=1\vee\max\left\{|F|:
 \begin{array}{l}
 F\subseteq G_1(h),\\
 \|x-x'\|_2\geq h/2\ \text{for distinct }x,x'\in F,\\
 a^U(x,h)\leq u(v)\ \text{for every }x\in F
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
Define the empirical lower-mass severity of \(g\in G_1(h)\) by
\[
 \widehat u(g,h)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a^L(g,h)=0,\\
 \min\{v\in U_n\setminus\{0\}:v\geq a^L(g,h)\},&a^L(g,h)>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(v\in U_n\), let
\(\mathcal G_1(h,v)=\{g\in G_1(h):\widehat u(g,h)=v\}\).
Scan \(\mathcal G_1(h,v)\) in increasing boundary-coordinate order and
retain a point if and only if its distance from every previously retained
point is at least \(h\).  The retained ordered set is
\(\mathcal A_1(h,v)\).  For \(x\in B\), put \(g=g_h(x)\) and
\(v=\widehat u(g,h)\), and let \(\gamma_1(x,h)\) be the first point of
\(\mathcal A_1(h,v)\) within distance strictly less than \(h\) of \(g\),
with \(g\) itself used when it is an anchor.

For \(g\in G_1(h)\), put
\[
 Z_n(g,h)=1+\log\!\left[
 e\widehat J\!\left(
 h,128\left\{\widehat u(g,h)+\frac{\ell_n}{m\vee1}\right\}\right)\right].
\]
Call \(h\) admissible if
\[
 n_2a^L(g,h)\geq2^{14}Z_n(g,h)
 \quad\text{for every }g\in G_1(h).
\]
Set
\[
 \widehat V(h)=
 \begin{cases}
 Lh+16\sigma\displaystyle\max_{g\in G_1(h)}
 \sqrt{\dfrac{Z_n(g,h)}{n_2a^L(g,h)}},
 &h\ \text{is admissible},\\[2ex]
 +\infty,&h\ \text{is not admissible}.
 \end{cases}
\]
If at least one bandwidth is admissible, let \(\widehat h\) be the smallest
minimizer of \(\widehat V(h)\) over \(h\in H_n\); otherwise put
\(\widehat h=h_0\).

On \(I_2\), for \(a\in B\), define
\[
 N^{(2)}_t(a,h)=\sum_{i\in I_2}
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\ \|X_i-a\|_2\leq h\},
\]
\[
 \widetilde Y^{(2)}_t(a,h)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&N^{(2)}_t(a,h)=0,\\[1ex]
 \dfrac{\sum_{i\in I_2}Y_i
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\ \|X_i-a\|_2\leq h\}}
 {N^{(2)}_t(a,h)},&N^{(2)}_t(a,h)>0,
 \end{cases}
\quad
 \overline Y^{(2)}_t(a,h)=\Pi_L(\widetilde Y^{(2)}_t(a,h)).
\]
The fixed-bandwidth anchor extension and the final estimator are
\[
 \widehat\tau_{n,h}(x)=
 \Pi_{2L}\!\left[
 \overline Y^{(2)}_1(\gamma_1(x,h),h)
 -\overline Y^{(2)}_0(\gamma_1(x,h),h)\right],
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat h}(x).
\]

proposed.justification: The global packing-oracle inequality makes thin-site multiplicity, with the necessary unit floor for empty profiles, determine the anchor maximum without an uncontrolled continuum.
proposed.gap: Existing inhomogeneous-design results do not give this measurable unweighted boundary-supremum oracle over the declared bivariate side-mass class.
proposed.consumer: Practitioners obtain one fully defined density-free causal-curve estimator without knowing the depletion exponent or support regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem claim, free-symbol closure, and dependency spine must match the corrected global-bandwidth definition and its new severity-net lemma.

proposed.statement:
Corollary (same-estimator consequence for the endpoint classes of
\(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\)).  There is a
finite constant \(C\), uniform over \(K\), such that for every
\(\kappa\in K\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), the single total estimator
\(\widehat\tau_n\), without knowledge of \(\kappa\) or the endpoint class,
satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq Cn^{-1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
proposed.justification: The two endpoint rates are obtained by evaluating the same global oracle at one common bandwidth for each class.
proposed.gap: The endpoint benchmarks did not previously come with one total exponent-free and profile-free estimator attaining both upper rates.
proposed.consumer: Analysts can use one causal boundary-curve procedure without selecting an isolated or pervasive support regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses the base-mass and packing definitions, so their dependencies are made explicit while the claim itself remains unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: A single split-sample estimator now closes the protected global-bandwidth oracle. The first half forms tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, partitions them into dyadic lower-mass bands, builds ordered greedy anchor nets, and selects one global bandwidth; the second half averages only at anchors and extends their clipped contrasts. The conditional maximum is therefore finite and controlled by \(1\vee J_P\), yielding the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) with the same \(\kappa\)-free estimator.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with vanishing one-sided mass needs a measurable estimator whose stochastic index set reflects thin-site multiplicity without importing the full continuum of local ball averages.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is a global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle over the declared bivariate side-mass class. It combines the tie-safe same-radius packing comparison with an explicit finite anchor extension.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors give geometrically increasing count scales and anchor cardinalities bounded by the floored empirical packing count. Conditional sub-Gaussian maxima then range only over anchors at one first-half-selected bandwidth, producing an honest \(\inf_h\sup_x\) oracle and simultaneous endpoint upper rates.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, dyadic lower-mass bands, ordered greedy anchors, empirical packing penalties, and one global bandwidth. Second-half outcomes are averaged only at anchors and the clipped contrasts are extended to all boundary points. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is parametrically estimated.

prose_updates.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation, whereas the present Lipschitz constant \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate designs with finitely many density zeros under spatially normalized loss. Those classes are neither included in nor supersets of the present bivariate side-mass class, so their theorems do not transfer directly. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu assume a continuous score density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. Only the conditionally sub-Gaussian overlap of that positive-density class is comparable with the regular subcase here; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Conversely, estimator-restricted lower bounds remain estimator-restricted. The same-radius comparison and severity-net extension used here are proved directly.
prose_updates.interpretation: At a fixed bandwidth, the first half learns both empirical severity and how many separated anchors occur at that severity. Assigning each boundary point to a nearby anchor in its own band costs only a constant multiple of \(Lh\). Because the second half evaluates no other centers, the stochastic supremum pays the local floored packing logarithm rather than the number of raw score-induced cells.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The oracle is deliberately global-bandwidth: its optimization order is \(\inf_h\sup_x\), not the stronger \(\sup_x\inf_h\). The result does not claim arbitrary-profile local-oracle exactness, point-dependent bandwidth adaptation, or exact simultaneous bands beyond the separately declared finite-pattern construction. Constants are uniform only on the compact exponent window bounded away from two.
prose_updates.honest_scope: This round proves the pure same-radius empirical-packing lemma, the finite empirical severity-net extension bound, the corrected global-bandwidth population oracle, and simultaneous isolated and pervasive endpoint upper rates. It preserves \(1\vee J_P\) at empty thin sets and handles breakpoint ties, zero second-half counts, empty admissible sets, and \(u=1\). It makes no claim for the discarded pointwise-bandwidth continuum argument and does not infer any arbitrary-profile or local-oracle band guarantee.

statement_notes.justification: The corrected theorem proves the profile-sensitive \(\inf_h\sup_x\) risk bound for an explicit one-bandwidth anchor-extension estimator.
statement_notes.gap: The former \(\sup_x\inf_h\) display was incompatible with one global bandwidth and relied on an unproved varying-radius maximal inequality.
statement_notes.consumer: The result supplies a total, measurable, exponent-free estimator whose stochastic penalty is computable from first-half anchor multiplicities.

statement_notes.justification: Common bandwidths at the isolated and pervasive balances evaluate the corrected oracle without changing either endpoint exponent.
statement_notes.gap: The missing step was simultaneous attainment by one profile-free estimator, not the endpoint rate calculation itself.
statement_notes.consumer: The same procedure can be deployed without a preliminary isolated-versus-pervasive regime choice.

statement_notes.justification: The lemma remains a pure first-half, tie-safe same-radius comparison with the mandatory unit floor.
statement_notes.gap: It does not itself make an outcome-risk assertion; that role is now discharged by the separate severity-net extension lemma.
statement_notes.consumer: The anchor construction uses its confidence bounds, pattern representative, and exact-radius population comparison.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma proves anchor coverage, packing-controlled anchor cardinality, and the conditional second-half maximum at one fixed bandwidth.
statement_notes.gap: It replaces the invalid exposed-arc population-mass substitution with direct binomial count control and conditional sub-Gaussian maxima over finite anchors.
statement_notes.consumer: The headline theorem applies it at the single first-half-measurable minimizer.
